title: The Saint
paragraphs: Radio adventures of Simon Templar, Leslie Charteris's charming and unconventional crime-fighter, played for much of the surviving run by Vincent Price.
Radio incarnations of Leslie Charteris' Simon Templar. network episodes, two collector-misdated Vincent Price copies, and three 1995 BBC Radio 4 adaptations.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: 1945 U.S. radio (January 6, 1945 to December 1, 1945), Price/Conway U.S. era (October 15, 1947 to July 15, 1951), and BBC Radio 4 adaptations (August 28, 1995 to September 11, 1995).

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Leslie Charteris (creator), [[person|vincent-price|Vincent Price]] (performer), James L. Saphier (producer), Merrill Ross (announcer and performer), Harry Zimmerman (composer and conductor), Barney Phillips (performer), and Dan O'Herlihy (performer).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], and [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].
The stories often return to crime and criminals, Simon Templar / The Saint, and detection and investigation.
The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Literary-to-radio franchise continuity, Vincent Price radio era, and BBC Radio 4 revival.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]], [[show|escape|Escape]], [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]], and [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]].
